name: Agency and office formation doctrine
purpose: Own the formation doctrine that relates persons, characters, models, sessions, agents, skills, duties, work, offices, cohorts, qualifications, incumbencies, and succession without copying the law of source settlements.

distinctions.person: a real human body; never inferred from a session or model
distinctions.character: the durable role-plus-disposition and dispositional nucleus through which a person or session becomes answerable; current Executive Office law keeps office membership and model identity elsewhere
distinctions.persona: a situated role and intention mask of a character for an audience, context, partner model, and work state; never the durable governor
distinctions.actor: a membrane-bounded public identity and affordance projection of a character and recorded session; an Agent Card advertises this surface rather than internal authority
distinctions.model-artifact: a versioned inference component; readiness evidence is not an officer qualification
distinctions.runtime-session: one ephemeral execution occurrence with exact context and resource history
distinctions.agent-relation: an inhabited runtime ecology over a recorded perceive-plan-act loop, persistent computable state, tools, context, and coordination; not a persona file
distinctions.skill: an invocable witnessed constructor with preconditions and postconditions, not a psychological trait
distinctions.duty: a standing obligation owed to a claim holder that passes whole across incumbents
distinctions.work: costly change that leaves the world different; not the skill used to perform it
distinctions.office: a durable normative body politic independent of its incumbent
distinctions.cohort: a branchable content-addressed formation epoch binding office, doctrine denominator, curriculum, exercises, assessment law, providers, and projectors while candidates progress asynchronously
distinctions.qualification: a scoped normal form over admitted evidence at one baseline and time, never authority
distinctions.incumbency: the receiving settlement's recognition-plus-induction act seating one character in one office
distinctions.succession: three distinct relations: incumbent handover, office replacement, and curriculum/baseline lineage

evidenceSettlement.rule: closure and four-valued settlement apply to the admitted evidence set, not to a person's mind or a model's weights
evidenceSettlement.qualificationRule: qualified requires demonstrated evidence for every baseline competency; contradiction, refutation, or absent evidence produces gaps or refusal
evidenceSettlement.historyRule: later correction, suspension, revocation, expiry, supersession, or requalification appends an event and never rewrites historical evidence

formationLaw: teach office, duty, work, skill, authority, capability, and appointment as non-equivalent relations
bind every customer overlay to exact owner, digest, jurisdiction, use grant, and egress terms
use situated progressive responsibility rather than attendance or task counts
require independent examination and negative controls
teach boundary refusal and succession, not only successful task performance
require clean-room context reconstruction for agent candidates so hidden session memory cannot substitute for curriculum
treat teaching-back as both learning evidence and an audit of whether practice is institutionally reproducible
derive learning evidence through observe, plan, evaluate, reflect, procedural memory, skill retrieval, and hook feedback
compose purpose-specific context carriers and record omissions instead of inventing a universal packet
treat current-practitioner lecturer and developmental mentor as engagement roles unless a distinct continuous Academy obligation later warrants an office
rejectedLegacyClaims: training is literally monotone, extensive, or idempotent over a person or neural model
task counts or confidence thresholds automatically promote a candidate
certification authorizes or appoints an officer
automation of a traversal retires the durable office obligation
a model, prompt, provider, harness, or runtime inherits another candidate's qualification
